speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah
text: asked	the Minister for Transport (a) whether LTA is aware of the many complaints regarding real-time updates on the MRT service breakdown for commuters on 28 June 2017; (b) what is being done to address commuters' need for timely and accurate information; and (c) whether LTA monitors the service standards of MRT train operators on the level of public engagement when there is a service breakdown.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I am quite sure you will settle down in your new responsibilities much quicker than I do in my transport portfolio.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The North-South Line has switched to a new signalling system which has been undergoing full-day testing since 28 May, that is, about four months ago.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The East-West Line is, however, still on the old signalling system, except for the new stretch between Joo Koon and Tuas West.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: So, I hope Members can visualise the complications: North-South Line, new signal; East-West Line, old signal; but one part is on new signal.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: As this occurred during the afternoon peak hour, many commuters were affected and their journeys delayed.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: The Singapore Mass Rapid Transit (SMRT) and Thales have since tightened their work processes to ensure that this does not happen again.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Basically, I told them, "Please suspend all major East-West Line testing until North-South Line has stabilised".

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: I reminded them that I am a heart patient and I do not want further shocks to my system.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Signs were also put up on other travel options, such as free bus services, and more than 3,200 announcements were made in stations and trains to keep commuters updated.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: Real-time updates were also broadcasted via social media, websites and MyTransport.SG mobile app.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: These measures were activated as part of the rail operators' contingency plans.

speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Khaw Boon Wan)
text: LTA will use the commuter feedback from the 28 June incident to enhance the management of service disruptions by the rail operators.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Many of my residents were inconvenienced by the 28 June incident and also the subsequent few train service interruptions.

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: First, how is the progress of the re-signalling project?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Second, how long more before we can see it stabilising, so that residents would not have to be inconvenienced, especially during peak hours?

speaker: Er Dr Lee Bee Wah (Nee Soon)
text: Last, but not least, can we have more bus services that bring residents to the city or work directly, such as Bus 805E, so that when there is a breakdown, at least they do not have to, like a lot of my residents, fight their way to take the shuttle service to go to Khatib MRT station and later find out that there is no train service?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The progress has been much better than I had originally feared.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The re-signalling project is a very complicated project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I remember during the Committee of Supply (COS) debate, I shared with the House the feedback that we got from London Underground.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They went through similar difficulties when they re-signalled their Jubilee Line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They were the first one who warned us, "expect problems, expect troubles, expect yourself to be public enemy No 1".

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I brought their painful experience to this House and have been trying very hard to prepare the ground on all the various things that we may have to go through.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Precisely because of the London Underground's experience, we changed very substantially our original schedule as well as approach to doing this re-signalling project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We decided to do a lot more testing during engineering hours before we start launching testing that involves passengers inside the trains.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The original plan was actually to start the full testing of the North-South Line much earlier than 28 May, which was our final decision.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We decided to change it and did a lot more testing during engineering hours when the trains were without passengers.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It was only after we have repeated testings and discovered many of the glitches and fixed them and were satisfied with the software before we start launching it to passenger service.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Even then, we take a step-by-step approach − trying out, first of all, during the last hour before service ends and, after that, during Sundays when the passenger load is a lot lighter.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We picked 28 May obviously because of the June holidays.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But unfortunately, despite all these preparations, there were still delays.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But over time, because of these various efforts that we have put in, the picture is getting better.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have about 10 weeks left to December.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I see no reason why we cannot deliver on this.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The new software that we put in since 14 July has been very promising, but there are still a few hardware problems.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Some of the equipment which are on the trains are still causing us some difficulties.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is not significant, but nevertheless, they are glitches which we have to fix.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Some of the glitches are: the doors are not opening or synchronising with the platform screen doors, or the trains exceed by a certain distance when it stops at the station.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I hope Members appreciate the complications of this project because, unlike a new line, let us say, Downtown Line 3, where there is also a new signalling system.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is a greenfield project, whereas this one, we are talking about an existing functioning line and we cannot close it down just to do testing.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: A further complication which the Thales engineers have explained is that because this is a 30-year-old system and, over the years, we have bought new trains.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, altogether today, we have four different generations of trains running on the North-South, East-West Lines.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And for the re-signalling, every train has to be completely rewired.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Each train is a little bit like a human being.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It has its own idiosyncrasies and we need plenty of time to calibrate and recalibrate.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: These are the great difficulties that all metros around the world experience when they need to re-signal.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But versus the experience of London Underground, honestly, for us who are involved in this project, we thought we have done much, much better than I originally envisaged.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: London took one full year before they stabilised.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For ours, we started in earnest since 28 May.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We have been installing the equipment and doing some testing during engineering hours.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I hope the experience that we have picked up on the North-South Line should be able to be put to use when we extend the re-signalling to the East-West Line, and that we do not need such a long period to stabilise the East-West Line.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As for bus services during disruptions, I think the honest answer is that a bus system is not as effective as trains during peak hours for the sheer difference in capacity.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: One train is equivalent to so many busloads of passenger capacity, and every two minutes, there is a new train coming.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, when there is an accumulation of delays, you can imagine we will need tens of thousands of buses to move or to transfer all the train passengers, and it is not easy.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: As for the Member's specific request for direct line bus to the Central Business District, we will take a look.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: First, I would like to ask the Minister whether he sets specific targets for the improvement of train service from the North-South Line, North-East Line, as well as other lines, because of different circumstances, as what the Minister mentioned.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Thirdly, I remember the Minister was quite optimistic when he took over and said that the MRT system will be improved over time.

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: Lastly, I would like to ask him: what can commuters expect in the future in terms of train services?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: How long more do they have to endure this inconvenience?

speaker: Mr Low Thia Khiang (Aljunied)
text: How long more before they can expect to see the light of the day and to have improvement and better efficiency in the train services?

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We are actually undergoing or carrying out two very different and separate missions.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The first mission is to raise the reliability of all existing lines.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The second mission is to do new projects, such as replacement of the signalling system, such as extending the Downtown Line to new stretches of the Downtown Line called Downtown Line 3.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Both are very different missions and we should not conflate the two.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: On the first one of raising reliability, we are making very good progress.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Reliability is measured by Mean Kilometres Between Failure (MKBF).

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The average distance in kilometres (km) travelled by a train before you hit a delay of more than five minutes.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And that is the global international standard of measuring reliability.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Low talked about my being optimistic when I first took over this job almost exactly two years ago.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I said I shall accomplish this job within four years and we are on track to accomplishing this project within four years.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: We are halfway through this journey and the MKBF improvements are significant and drastic.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For a long time, our MKBF could not even exceed 200,000 km.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Mr Low asked whether the Minister has a target.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: And I set those targets and recorded it in Hansard in this House.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: At that time, the best MKBF data was experienced by Taipei.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is ambitious, optimistic, but I have reason to be confident and I think even if we cannot reach it, we will be quite close to it.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because part of the efforts in improving reliability is to replace the very old assets.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The North-South, East-West Lines, 30 years old, are almost at the end of their economic life.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: That is why we have to progressively replace the assets.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But replacing the assets when we only have three hours every day, which is at midnight, takes a long time.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: For a system like the North-South, East-West Lines, there are six critical core systems.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Sleepers, third rail, signalling, trains, power supply, track circuits.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Each one has to be replaced before you can hope to improve on the reliability.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Third rail, I am doing an event tomorrow to celebrate the completion of third rail.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But East-West Line's signalling has yet to be done.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: So, basically, it is a multi-year effort, we are halfway there.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Next year, I will top it up further and I am fairly confident we will be able to deliver this mission.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It was in this House at COS when I explained the problem on the London Underground.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: As the Minister is aware, hundreds of rail engineers and technicians work hard every day, every night, to upgrade the MRT system.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: Sometimes, we do not even have the three hours that he spoke of at night.

speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Tanjong Pagar)
text: I hope to have the Minister's assurance that the Ministry in pursuing the high standards of MRT operations, the very high standards that he has set for the operators, that the Minister can continue to assure that the well-being of our rail workers will continue to be a top priority of the Ministry.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I spend a lot of time with our troops on the ground in the trenches within the tunnels, day time, night time, each time there is something to celebrate, I go down to celebrate with them, buy them some durians, buy them some curry puffs.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Little, small gestures, but I think it makes some difference to them as well as to me because I want to satisfy myself that people are not lazing around, giving excuses, but actually putting all their heart and soul into their projects – and they do.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: The reason why I spend time, and recently I have a little argument with the media, was because I feel for my people.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: They put so much effort, heart, sweat and tears into their project.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: I think the minimum they hope is that people will cheer them on rather than jeer at them.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Because it is a multi-year effort, it is like a war.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: Fighting a multi-year war, I think staff morale is key.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: If we are able to keep staff morale high, I think the success possibility will be high.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: It is so easy to feel discouraged and say let us quit.

speaker: Mr Khaw Boon Wan
text: But we have a job to do and we will deliver.
